title: useId
summary: **useId** is the React Hook that generates a stable, unique id string for a component instance — perfect for connecting accessibility attributes like a label's `htmlFor` to an input's `id` without collisions, even across server and client renders.

subtopics.title: Accessibility ids
subtopics.explanation: A label can point to an input by using the same id. Screen readers then know which label describes the field. It is like putting the same tracking number on a package and its receipt.

subtopics.title: Label/input association
subtopics.explanation: Set a label's `htmlFor` to the input's `id`. When the visitor clicks the label, the input receives focus. The shared id works like a name tag linking the two.

subtopics.title: ARIA attributes
subtopics.explanation: Some accessibility attributes use ids to point to help text or error messages. `useId` can create those connections. It is like cross-referencing a form field with its instruction card.

subtopics.title: SSR-stable ids
subtopics.explanation: Server rendering creates HTML before the browser runs React. `useId` helps the server and browser produce matching ids, preventing a mismatch. It is like using the same numbered form in two offices.

subtopics.title: Hydration
subtopics.explanation: Hydration is when React connects behavior to HTML that already arrived from the server. The first browser render must match that HTML. It is like attaching controls to a finished display without changing its labels.

subtopics.title: Id suffixes
subtopics.explanation: Call `useId` once, then add clear suffixes for related elements, such as `-label` and `-hint`. This keeps each id distinct. It is like one folder number with separate tabs.

subtopics.title: Not for list keys
subtopics.explanation: Do not use `useId` to create keys for list items. Keys must come from the data and stay tied to each item. A `useId` value is for connecting page elements, like a label to a field.

foundations.overview: `useId` creates an id that connects related elements, such as a form label and its input. React keeps the id stable across server and browser rendering. Think of it as a matching number printed on two linked forms.
foundations.formalDefinition: useId is a React Hook that returns a unique, deterministic id string for the calling component: `const id = useId()`. The value is stable across re-renders of that component instance and is generated identically on the server and the client so it survives hydration.
foundations.whyItMatters: Accessible forms require ids that link controls to their labels and descriptions. Hardcoding ids breaks when a component is rendered more than once on a page, and random ids break server-side rendering. useId solves both problems with one call.
foundations.mentalModel: Think of useId as React handing each component instance a unique name tag based on its position in the component tree. Wherever that component appears — once or a hundred times — each instance gets its own tag, and React promises the same tag on the server and the browser.
foundations.browserPerspective: The id useId returns is written into the real DOM as an attribute (for example id=":r1:"). Screen readers and the browser's accessibility tree read these attributes to connect a label to its field. The exact string is opaque on purpose — you should never parse it or rely on its format.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Connecting a label to an input via htmlFor/id, linking a field to its help or error text via aria-describedby, and giving reusable form components their own ids so they can be dropped onto a page multiple times without conflicts.
foundations.businessImpact: Inaccessible forms exclude users who rely on assistive technology and create legal and compliance risk. useId makes correct, accessible markup the easy default, which protects both users and the business.
foundations.engineeringImpact: useId removes a whole class of bugs caused by duplicate or mismatched ids and lets teams ship truly reusable form components instead of one-off markup with hand-picked ids.
foundations.performanceImpact: useId is effectively free at runtime — it computes a string once per component instance and does not trigger extra renders. It also prevents hydration mismatches, which would otherwise force React to throw away server HTML and re-render on the client.
commonUseCases: Linking a <label> to an <input> with matching htmlFor and id
Connecting a field to help text or an error message via aria-describedby
Building reusable form-field components that can appear many times on a page
Generating ids for related elements (a field plus its hint) from one base id using suffixes

commonMisconceptions.myth: useId is for generating keys in a list.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It is not. List keys should come from your data (a stable item id). useId returns the same value across renders of one instance, so it cannot distinguish list items.

commonMisconceptions.myth: You can use Math.random() or an array index instead.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Math.random() differs between the server and client renders, causing hydration mismatches, and changes on every render; indexes collide when a component is reused. useId is stable and SSR-safe.

visualExplorer.title: How useId produces a stable, accessible id
visualExplorer.caption: Step through how one useId call flows into matching label/input attributes and survives server-to-client hydration.

steps.title: Component renders
steps.description: A form-field component renders and calls const id = useId() to ask React for a unique id.

steps.title: React assigns an id
steps.description: React derives a deterministic id from the component's position in the tree, e.g. ":r1:", and returns the same string on every re-render of this instance.

steps.title: Wire up the markup
steps.description: Set <label htmlFor={id}> and <input id={id}>. The browser now knows the label describes that input.

steps.title: Add related ids with suffixes
steps.description: Build extra ids from the base, like {id}-hint, and point aria-describedby at the hint element — one useId call, several linked elements.

steps.title: Server renders the same id
steps.description: During server-side rendering React generates the identical id string, so the HTML sent to the browser already has the correct attributes.

steps.title: Hydration matches
steps.description: On the client React produces the same id again, the markup matches the server HTML, and hydration succeeds with no mismatch warning.

interactiveExamples.title: A label connected to its input
interactiveExamples.explanation: useId() returns a unique string. Using it for both the label's htmlFor and the input's id links them, so clicking the label focuses the field and screen readers announce the label.
interactiveExamples.expectedOutput: A labeled email input where clicking the label moves focus into the field.

interactiveExamples.title: One id, multiple linked elements
interactiveExamples.explanation: A single useId call gives you a base string. Add suffixes to create related ids — here the field plus its hint — and wire them with aria-describedby so assistive tech reads the hint with the input.
interactiveExamples.expectedOutput: A password field whose hint is programmatically associated via aria-describedby using a suffixed id.

codeLab.title: Build an accessible labeled field
codeLab.instructions: Use useId to create one unique id. Connect the <label> to the <input> with htmlFor/id, and connect the help text to the input with aria-describedby using a suffix of the same id.
codeLab.expectedOutput: Clicking the label focuses the input, and the help text is linked via aria-describedby.
hints: Call const id = useId() at the top of the component.
Set htmlFor={id} on the label and id={id} on the input so they match.
Build the help-text id with a template literal like `${id}-help` and reference it from aria-describedby.

keyTakeaways: useId returns a unique, stable id string per component instance for wiring up accessibility attributes.
Use it for label htmlFor/input id and for aria-describedby links to help or error text.
Never use Math.random() or array indexes — they break hydration or collide when components are reused.
Call useId once and add suffixes (e.g. `${id}-hint`) to create several related ids from one base.
useId is SSR-safe: it generates the same id on the server and client so hydration matches.
It is not for list keys — use a stable id from your data for those.
